# FlightGear A320-family: corresponding source notices (GPL-2.0 only)

This directory holds the **licence and copyright notices** of the FlightGear "A320-family" project, from which libresim derives its A320 flight-model data (and, in a later phase, models and textures). The data itself is not copied here: it is fetched into `data/raw/fg/a320` (gitignored) by `tools/22_a320_fetch.sh`, pinned to the commit below, and published as part of the A320 pack source.

- **Upstream:** https://github.com/legoboyvdlp/A320-family (mirror: https://git.nayala.duckdns.org/fly/A320-family)
- **Branch / commit:** `dev`, commit `fec1ecba767c8fffd145337b27012e89c01e3ade` (committed 2026-09-25)
- **Fetched:** 2026-10-28 (`tools/22_a320_fetch.sh`: shallow sparse checkout of that exact commit)
- **Licence:** **GNU GPL version 2 only** ("under the terms of version 2 ... as published by the Free Software Foundation": no "or later"). Text in `LICENSE`. Consequence: a distribution that contains these files (or works derived from them) is GPL-2.0 as a whole; libresim's own code is GPL-2.0-or-later, which allows this combination, but the combined result cannot be relicensed under GPLv3.
- **Copyright (from `README.copyright.md`, reproduced verbatim in this directory):** Copyright (c) 2025 Josh Davidson, Jonathan Redpath, merspieler, Matthew Maring, Thorsten Herrmann, Semir Gebran. Individual files carry their own newer lines (for example `A320-main.xml`: "Copyright (c) 2026 Josh Davidson (Octal450) and Matthew Maring (mattmaring)"); every upstream copyright line stays in the data files, which are never edited in place.
- **Authors (from the `<authors>` block of `A320-main.xml`):** Josh Davidson / Octal450 (flight dynamics, systems, instruments), Jonathan Redpath / legoboyvdlp (systems, instruments, FMGC), Nia (systems, instruments), Matthew Maring / mattmaring (fuel predictions, FMGC), Thorsten Herrmann / TH-555 (cockpit 3D model), Semir Gebran / CaptB (3D model), Andrea Vezzali / vezza (systems, instruments).
- **Base aircraft:** credited upstream (`THANKS.md`) to Immersive Design Group ("the aircraft this is based on"). See "Residual risk" below.

## What is taken, and what is not
Taken (phase P1; sparse checkout, ~2.5 MB):
- `FDE/` (JSBSim flight dynamics), `Engines/` (JSBSim engine and thruster files), `Systems/` (JSBSim systems, including the fly-by-wire files), the top-level `A320-200-CFM-set.xml` and the other top-level files that come with a cone checkout, `LICENSE`, `README.copyright.md`, `Docs/THANKS.md`.
- Models and textures (`Models/`, phase P8, 2026-10-28): only the subset listed in the change log below and in the header of `tools/24_a320_models_fetch.sh` (about 87 MB at the pinned commit).

Excluded on purpose, not fetched, not shipped, not credited as used (licence audit, see `docs/LICENSING.md`):
- `Sounds/`: no per-file provenance; the announcement voices are text-to-speech output of an unchecked service; two upstream sound pull requests were rejected over provenance.
- `Fonts/`: the ECAM font is credited upstream only as "GPL" and comes from FlyByWire (GPLv3 code, CC-BY-NC assets).
- Anything from **FlyByWire A32NX**.
- `Nasal/` and `WebPanel/` code: libresim writes its own displays and logic from public behaviour of the aircraft, not by porting this code.
- Real airline liveries (AAL, AUA, DAL, SWR) and any Airbus, airline or engine-maker logos and decals; navdata; the splash screen.
- The CC0 sample listed in `THANKS.md` (Amanda Santos, "botaodepressao") is **not used**; `THANKS.md` is reproduced unchanged because it is an upstream notice.

## Change log (GPLv2 section 2a: prominent, dated notice of changes)
libresim never edits the upstream files. Files derived from them are generated by scripts, so the notice is part of each output and of this list:
- 2026-10-28: `game/aircraft/a320/config.json` and `aero.json` are generated from `FDE/A320-200-CFM.xml` and `Engines/cfm56-5b4_*.xml` by `tools/06_jsbsim_to_json.py a320` (unit conversion to SI, XML to JSON expression trees, tables kept; features the converter cannot translate are listed in the JSON under `unconverted`). Both files carry a `"derived_from"` field naming the upstream files and commit.
- 2026-10-28 (P8, models): `tools/24_a320_models_fetch.sh` adds `Models/Fuselage/` (exterior AC3D, engine AC3D, textures, animation XML read as data), `Models/FlightDeck/res/` (flight deck AC3D and textures), `Models/Lights/`, the 481-byte display-screen quads of `Models/Instruments/{PFD,ND,Upper-ECAM,Lower-ECAM,IESI}/res/` and four single files (`A320-common.xml`, `A320-200-CFM.xml`, `Liveries/CFM/2k/CFM56-white.png` (the unliveried engine texture), see the script header) to the sparse checkout; no liveries, no `Instruments/` Nasal/canvas files, no `Effects/`, no sounds.
- 2026-10-28 (P8, models): `game/aircraft/a320/models/exterior.glb` is generated from `Models/Fuselage/res/A320-216.ac` and `CFM56.ac` by `tools/blender/convert_a320.py` (own AC3D reader `tools/blender/ac3d_parse.py`; Blender 5.2.3): converted AC3D to glTF; rebuilt all materials as Principled BSDF; dropped FlightGear-only and hidden meshes (door / cargo / wheel-well interiors, actuators and linkages, placards, navigation-light glass, the WingtipFence variant, the blurred fan discs, windscreen wipers); split the animated parts into `pivot_<part>` nodes with hinge axes taken from upstream's animation XML (`tools/blender/a320_hinges.py`); merged the static parts into one mesh; smooth shading by angle. No geometry was edited or remodelled otherwise.
- 2026-10-28 (P8, models): textures are derived by `tools/24_a320_textures.py`: the fuselage atlas (`Fuse-Main.png`, an unliveried template) is recoloured to plain white with a slate cheat line, the template's registration "N680AW" (both sides) is erased to a flat fill, black and blue template placeholders on the fin and belly fairing are painted white; the tyre sidewall lettering ("FlightGear", a tyre-maker mark) of `LandingGears.png` is removed; the engine texture is `CFM56-white.png` unchanged; flight-deck textures are reduced to at most 2048 px and the "Airbus A320 Family" legend on `fd_main.png` is painted over. No Airbus, airline or engine-maker mark is knowingly left (no OCR available: the checks were by eye on every texture sheet at reduced size; small placard text in the flight-deck sheets was not read line by line).
- 2026-10-28 (P8, models): `game/aircraft/a320/models/interior.glb` is generated from `Models/FlightDeck/res/fd_complete.ac` (and the five display-screen quads) by `tools/blender/convert_a320_cockpit.py`: converted to glTF, rebuilt materials, dropped seats, headsets, tablets, HUD and IAE variants, the rear cabin and the Nasal-driven screen sockets, planar-dissolved and collapse-decimated to about 95k triangles, display quads kept as plain black meshes `screen_<name>` for libresim's own displays.

## Residual risk (stated plainly)
The upstream authors may not have been able to license the parts derived from Immersive Design Group's A32X, and our changes do not alter that. libresim uses the licence the repository publishes (GPL-2.0 for the whole repository), complies with it in full, and keeps the A320 as a separate, withdrawable pack whose model can be replaced by an own generic twin-jet without code changes.

## Trademarks
"Airbus" and "A320" are trademarks of Airbus. libresim is not affiliated with or endorsed by Airbus or any airline or engine maker; it uses a generic livery and no real operator marks.

## Rebuilding
1. `tools/22_a320_fetch.sh` (idempotent; `--force` re-fetches).
2. `tools/.venv/bin/python tools/06_jsbsim_to_json.py a320`.
3. Models: `tools/24_a320_models_fetch.sh`, `tools/.venv/bin/python -I tools/24_a320_textures.py`, then both Blender scripts and `tools/24_a320_sections.py` (docs/USAGE.md "A320 model").
